match.reason: None of the bank points explains why carbon's four valence electrons and strong bonding give it millions of compounds; the closest, Allotropes, covers different structural forms of carbon, which is a related but different idea.

draft.title: Why carbon is special
card: A carbon atom has four valence electrons, the electrons in its outer shell. It shares each one in a covalent bond, so it forms four bonds.
Carbon forms strong covalent bonds with other carbon atoms. This lets it join into long chains, branched chains and rings.
Carbon also bonds strongly with other non-metal atoms, such as hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen and the halogens.
Four bonds per atom, plus the many ways to join atoms, give millions of different carbon compounds. Few other elements form such varied compounds.
draft.remember: Four bonds and strong C to C links let carbon build millions of compounds.

a.q: Which property of carbon atoms best explains why there are so many carbon compounds?
opts: They form four bonds and can bond strongly to each other
They form ionic bonds with most other elements
They have a full outer shell and so bond very easily
They form two bonds and so can only make short chains
a.why: Four covalent bonds per atom, and strong bonds between carbon atoms, allow chains, branches and rings in many arrangements. A carbon atom has four valence electrons, not a full outer shell, so it needs to share electrons.
a.clue: Think about how many bonds each atom makes and what it can bond to.

b.q: A chemist says that carbon can form branched chains and rings. Which feature of carbon makes this possible?
opts: Each atom can make four bonds, including bonds to carbon
Each atom can lose four electrons to form an ion
Each atom has four electron shells to hold bonds
Each atom can make bonds only with hydrogen atoms
b.why: Because each carbon atom makes four bonds and can bond strongly to other carbon atoms, chains can branch or close into rings. Carbon has four valence electrons, not four shells, and it shares electrons rather than losing them.
b.clue: Look at how many bonds each atom makes and what it can bond to.

a.best: They form four bonds and can bond strongly to each other

b.best: Each atom can make four bonds, including bonds to carbon
